sequences.title: Opaque Capability Negotiation and Selective Flooding

intro.quote: When opaque-capable routers and non-opaque-capable OSPF routers are mixed together in a routing domain, the Opaque LSAs are typically not flooded to the non-opaque-capable routers.

steps.explain: The router floods Opaque LSAs only to opaque-capable neighbors. A non-capable neighbor may still receive a multicast Link State Update and discards the Opaque LSA.

cite.quote: Opaque LSAs MUST be placed on the link-state retransmission lists of opaque-capable neighbors and MUST NOT be placed on the link-state retransmission lists of non-opaque-capable neighbors. However, when sending Link State Update packets as multicasts, a non-opaque-capable neighbor may (inadvertently) receive Opaque LSAs. The non-opaque-capable router will then simply discard the LSA (see Section 13 of [OSPF] regarding receiving LSAs having unknown LS types).

intro.quote: Opaque LSAs contain some number of octets (of application-specific data) padded to 32-bit alignment. Like any other LSA, the Opaque LSA uses the link-state database distribution mechanism for flooding this information throughout the topology.

fields.name: LS age
fields.explain: The age carried by the link-state advertisement.

fields.name: Options
fields.explain: The standard LSA header's Options field, used to communicate optional OSPF capabilities.

cite.quote: The Options field enables OSPF routers to support (or not support) optional capabilities, and to communicate their capability level to other OSPF routers.

fields.name: Opaque Type
fields.explain: The first 8 bits of the link-state ID carry the Opaque type.

cite.quote: The link-state ID of the Opaque LSA is divided into an Opaque Type field (the first 8 bits) and an Opaque ID (the remaining 24 bits).

fields.name: Opaque ID
fields.explain: The remaining 24 bits of the link-state ID carry the type-specific Opaque ID.

cite.quote: The link-state ID of the Opaque LSA is divided into an Opaque Type field (the first 8 bits) and an Opaque ID (the remaining 24 bits).

fields.name: Opaque Information
fields.explain: Holds variable-length application-specific data and is padded to 32-bit alignment.

intro.quote: The Options field enables OSPF routers to support (or not support) optional capabilities, and to communicate their capability level to other OSPF routers.

fields.name: DN-bit
fields.explain: Prevents looping in BGP/MPLS IP VPNs.

cite.quote: DN-bit This bit is used to prevent looping in BGP/MPLS IP VPNs, as specified in [RFC4576].

fields.name: O-bit
fields.explain: Indicates willingness to receive and forward Opaque LSAs.

cite.quote: O-bit This bit describes the router's willingness to receive and forward Opaque LSAs as specified in this document.

fields.name: DC-bit
fields.explain: Describes the router's handling of demand circuits.

cite.quote: DC-bit This bit describes the router's handling of demand circuits, as specified in [DEMD].

fields.name: EA-bit
fields.explain: Indicates willingness to receive and forward External-Attributes-LSAs; its defining documents have expired.

cite.quote: EA-bit This bit describes the router's willingness to receive and forward External-Attributes-LSAs. While defined, the documents specifying this bit have all expired. The use of this bit may be deprecated in the future.

fields.name: N/P-bit
fields.explain: Describes the handling of Type-7 LSAs.

cite.quote: N/P-bit This bit describes the handling of Type-7 LSAs, as specified in [NSSA].

fields.name: MC-bit
fields.explain: Describes whether IP multicast datagrams are forwarded according to MOSPF.

cite.quote: MC-bit This bit describes whether IP multicast datagrams are forwarded according to the specifications in [MOSPF].

fields.name: E-bit
fields.explain: Describes the way AS-External LSAs are flooded.

cite.quote: E-bit This bit describes the way AS-External LSAs are flooded, as described in Sections 3.6, 9.5, 10.8, and 12.1.2 of [OSPF].

fields.name: MT-bit
fields.explain: Describes the router's multi-topology link-excluding capability.

cite.quote: MT-bit This bit describes the router's multi-topology link-excluding capability, as described in [OSPF-MT].
